chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Sayf, from his father, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever has children who precede him (to the afterlife), they will be reckoned in the Presence of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as a veil for him from the Fire, by the Permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.قَدَّمَ: To precede or go before (in death)

ai.seo_question: How do deceased children protect their parents from Hellfire according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the concept of 'qadam al-walad,' where deceased children act as an intercessory veil (hijab) shielding their parents from the Hellfire by God's permission. This tradition underscores the profound spiritual merit of parental devotion and the reciprocal mercy in the afterlife, a key theme in Shia eschatology regarding family ties. It serves as a source of comfort for bereaved parents, framing the loss not merely as a tragedy but as a divine gift of protection.
